messages:
Tom F (Finance Ops): FYI customer 'NordicApps' raised an escalation — invoice paid via Dedicated Entity A, but they need local-currency invoice for Entity B + PO.
Ken S (Support): On it. Customer says card was charged but their AP system flagged rounding mismatch: invoice shows EUR 1,234.56 but payment posted as EUR 1,234.58
Maya L (Acct Exec): They do cross-entity billing — payments flow to our USD centralized account, they need invoice in NOK for their local ledger and PO number on the header.
Olivia B (Billing): That NOK requirement is new for this account? We have multi-entity enabled but maybe currency conversion rounding is applied at settlement.
Ken S (Support): Repro steps from customer: 1) Create usage snapshot for entity-B 2) Request invoice in NOK 3) PO #5678 attached 4) Attempt to reconcile, AP reports 0.02 NOK difference -> block
Tom F (Finance Ops): Sounds like FX rounding at two places: platform invoice conversion vs payment processor settlement. Can we pull the raw converted amounts?
Olivia B (Billing): I pulled the invoice json: ```{"entity":"B","currency":"NOK","total_local":123456,"total_display":"NOK 1,234.56","fx_rate":"0.087645"}``` Not great formatting but shows conversion
Ken S (Support): Customer also saw a declined card on an earlier attempt — payment gateway returned CC_402_DECLINED_3DS. They retried and succeeded but amounts differ.
Maya L (Acct Exec): Customer legal insists invoice vendor and remit-to must match entity in PO, otherwise their AP blocks payment. They want a corrected invoice in NOK tied to entity B.
Tom F (Finance Ops): Action items: Olivia to generate corrected invoice with PO on header + explicit FX rate line; Finance to check settlement report to reconcile 0.02 NOK; Support to provide payment gateway trace for CC_402.
Olivia B (Billing): Will do. I'll attach corrected invoice and a note about rounding policy. ETA 2 business days. :white_check_mark:
InvoiceBot: Invoice 2024-09-23-987 gen for entity-B queued (id inv_8f7ab).
Ken S (Support): I'll follow up with the customer and confirm whether they need VAT/Tax breakdown on invoice too — some EU entities require VAT ids in local currency invoices.
Tom F (Finance Ops): Good call — include VAT lines if present. Keep this thread updated.
